item.title: Eagles release Pro Bowl quarterback Andy Dalton after just one disastrous pass in loss
item.description: Andy Dalton threw just one pass for the Philadelphia Eagles before his release, with Tanner McKee now taking over as the backup quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Eagles saw Andy Dalton throw one pass and decided they'd seen enough.

Dalton, 38, entered the Eagles’ 27-7 Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears after Jalen Hurts briefly left the game with an injury. The Eagles were down 7-0 in the second quarter and faced third-and-goal from the Bears' 2-yard line.

The three-time Pro Bowler took the shotgun snap but threw an interception when rookie safety Dillon Thieneman jumped the pass. On Friday, before the team departed for London, the Eagles released Dalton.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After Dalton’s interception, the Eagles promoted Tanner McKee to the backup quarterback role, dropping the former Cincinnati Bengals star to No. 3 on the depth chart. Now, he is no longer with the team.

The Eagles were the sixth team Dalton played for during his NFL career . He was a starter for the first nine years of his career with the Bengals but has since served as a backup for several teams.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Following his nine-year run with the Bengals, the three-time Pro Bowler played for the Dallas Cowboys (one season), Chicago Bears (one season), New Orleans Saints (one season), Carolina Panthers (three seasons) and Eagles.

Dalton had started games for every team he played for except the Eagles.

Dalton has played in 180 games, starting 169 of them, and has compiled an 84-83-2 record. He has completed 62.6% of his passes for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns and 152 interceptions.

The Eagles (2-2) will play the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) in London at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

item.title: Israeli combat medicine slashes IDF deaths after Oct 7, draws US military interest
item.description: IDF battlefield medicine cut combat mortality rates from 15% to 7.1%, with advances in casualty evacuation and trauma care now benefiting the U.S. Army.
item.content:encoded:
JERUSALEM — The growing number of Israeli army battlefield life-saving measures have emerged during the Iranian regime-backed multi-front war against the Jewish state that those new technologies are helping the U.S. too.

Fox News Digital was briefed on the most current insights and data on Israel’s success rate in saving soldiers’ lives from a senior Israel Defense Forces (IDF) medical specialist in battlefield medicine.

The grueling Israeli ground offensive against the U.S.-designated terrorist movement Hamas in the Gaza Strip, which started in Oct. 2023, following the Jihadi organization’s invasion of Israel on Oct. 7, introduced cutting-edge medical tactics to the battlefield.

THE US-ISRAEL STRATEGIC ALLIANCE – PARTNERSHIP, NOT CHARITY

Hamas brutally murdered over 1,200 people in southern Israel, including more than forty Americans, and kidnapped 251 people.

An IDF spokesman laid out the new advances: "The IDF Medical Corps adapted its operational capabilities during the war, including casualty evacuation, innovative medical technologies and providing treatment under fire in a challenging terrain. "

The IDF medical specialist told Fox News Digital that during "the Second War in Lebanon [in 2006 against the Lebanese-based terrorist group Hezbollah] it took 15 to 20 minutes for advanced life support to reach a casualty. Now advanced life support can reach a casualty immediately or within 4 minutes."

The placement of "medical personnel on the battlefield, including a doctor in every company, allows the IDF to make critical decisions early on during the care process," said the IDF medical specialist. The use of helicopters to deliver seriously wounded soldiers to medical facilities, as seen in video footage provided to Fox News Digital, plays a critical role in preventing death.

The second advance is, according to the IDF medical specialist, "rapid evacuation," which means "We can evacuate casualties to Israeli hospitals rapidly."

5 OF AMERICA'S GREATEST MEDICAL BREAKTHROUGHS REVEALED AS THE NATION MARKS 250 YEARS

There has been "an emphasis on the use of blood products since 2013 on stopping bleeding," said the IDF medical specialist. He added that the IDF is the first medical organization that "used plasma on the point of injury instead of salt and water."

He noted the IDF implemented a sophisticated rapid-fire system for providing blood to injured soldiers. A telling example: Blood was placed on the back of first responders in coolers to stop bleeding and control the hemorrhaging. The method "saved significant numbers" of injured soldiers.

An additional improvement in lifesaving first response medicine in the war zone involves an "advanced system of learning and the collection of data that transmits the data over technical networks so that every provider can see patient data."

The IDF specialist said that "Every relevant medical officer on the chain can see the patient data. This system had very good results."

The case mortality rate is the best index for quantifying care, said the IDF medical specialist. The results have been dramatic. According to IDF data, the mortality rate during the 2006 war against Hezbollah was 15% in contrast to 7.1% during 2023. 

The IDF medical specialist said Israel’s military medicine apparatus has relied on the bedrock 2012 U.S. study "Death on the battlefield (2001–2011): Implications for the future of combat casualty care," which covered American medical aid during the war in Iraq.

Dr. Marc Siegel, senior medical analyst for Fox News, is also a clinical professor of medicine and a practicing internist at NYU Langone Medical Center, told Fox News Digital, "Battle field advances based on the latest technologies that have been developed in Israel, including surgical techniques as well as the latest burn treatment Nexobrid help not just today’s wounded but fuel medical and surgical advances around the world."  

Siegel's latest book "The Angels Among Us: How God's Messengers Play a Role in Healing," features a chapter involving a medical rescue during the Gaza war.

The U.S. Army and the IDF have been cooperating in how to advance battlefield medicine for years.

MICHIGAN MILITARY EXERCISE PREPARING THOUSANDS OF TROOPS FOR CHANGING BATTLEFIELD

According to an April 2026 U.S. military report titled "Israeli Defense Force Medical Lessons Learned," the American military authors explained in the 78-page study the pressing need to absorb Israel’s advances from the start of the Swords of Iron War campaign in 2023.

The U.S. Army wrote, "In the fields of operational health and force readiness, the IDF executed proactive public health measures – including robust bio-surveillance, forward-positioned preventive medicine teams and stringent food safety protocols – to mitigate health threats and maintain operational readiness."

The American army warned that "Despite Israel’s preparations, it had to undergo a painful process of transformation in contact that the U.S. now has the opportunity to avoid. The time for preparation is now. Simply possessing clinical and tactical skills is insufficient."

An IDF spokesman told Fox News Digital that the U.S. Army study of Israel's emergency health care providers during the wars" was a joint collaboration, and American officers came to learn from the IDF."

item.title: Arch Manning ranked fifth among 2027 NFL Draft quarterbacks as exec questions 'blind faith' based off name
item.description: Arch Manning ranked fifth in ESPN's 2027 NFL Draft quarterback rankings as one AFC executive questioned the "blind faith" surrounding his ceiling.
item.content:encoded:
Arch Manning is focused on helping his No. 1 Texas Longhorns reach the College Football Playoff, and hopefully, the national championship game this season, but many are focused on what he does at the next level of his football career.

Manning, the nephew of NFL great quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning, has been carrying that weight since he was in high school as a top prospect. But while there have been flashes of greatness from the Longhorns signal caller, ESPN’s latest quarterback rankings for the stacked 2027 NFL Draft have him at No. 5.

In fact, one AFC assistant general manager told the outlet that Manning seems to have created "this blind faith" due to his namesake.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"What’s giving so many people this blind faith that there’s just this monstrous ceiling with him?" the executive questioned. "Maybe this current state is just who he really is as a prospect."

Manning entered the 2026 college season with something to prove after what some viewed as an underwhelming 2025 campaign. He threw for 3,163 yards with 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 13 games.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This season, Manning has thrown for 862 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions for his 4-0 Longhorns, which includes a 21-point fourth-quarter comeback against Ohio State earlier this season.

The expectations for Manning, though, coming into college were as astronomical as you may think given the quarterbacks with the same name that came before him. He hasn’t hit those high expectations on a consistent basis, but there’s still lots of football left to play.

But as NFL teams have already begun the rigorous scouting period ahead of next year’s draft in April, every throw, pre-snap check and more for Manning, and the other top quarterback prospects, mean that much more.

For now, one AFC scout told ESPN that Manning is someone a team might "fall in love with" down the road – not necessarily right now.

"He’s always be graded on a different scale because of the name," the scout admitted. "…I don’t think he’s the best in the class, but his flashes in games are fascinating and a preview of what could happen down the road."

We’ve seen time and time again how prospects can change their draft stock with performances throughout a season. Even the NFL Scouting Combine changes the minds of all teams watching.

But Manning is expected to be in a draft class for the ages, with top quarterbacks like Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker, Miami’s Darian Mensah, Ole Miss’ Trinidad Chambliss, and Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, who were all ranked higher than him in ESPN’s latest list.

Manning has opportunities to change those perceptions in the upcoming weeks, facing five straight ranked opponents after the "Red River Rivalry" game against Oklahoma on Saturday. Texas is set to face No. 16 Florida, No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 17 Mississippi State, No. 14 Missouri and No. 10 LSU, respectively.

item.title: Frustrated Arkansas football fans float wild plan to get AD fired, and it could happen today
item.description: Arkansas fans are plotting to storm the field win or lose against Tennessee to rack up $250,000 NCAA fines and force Hunter Yurachek's firing.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a brutal year for Arkansas football.

Well, scratch that. It's been a brutal ... decade ... for Arkansas football.

The Razorbacks sit at 2-3 and near the bottom of the SEC ahead of today's matchup was Tennessee, and the prospects don't look great. The Vols (4-1) are No. 15 in the country, and are better than Arkansas in just about every metric possible.

ARKANSAS CAMPUS RESEMBLES A GHOST TOWN AS NO ONE SHOWS UP TO WATCH RAZORBACKS GET BEATEN DOWN BY GEORGIA

By all accounts, it should be a blowout — most Razorback losses this season have been. There's little reason to believe today will be any different.

But, there is some good news! Win OR lose (probably lose), fans are still mulling perhaps the most diabolical plan known to man to get AD Hunter Yurachek fired ...

Storm the field, and rack up the fines:

"Win or lose we #stormthefield Every game ends in a field storming and a $250,000 fine until @ArkRazorbacks fire @HunterYurachek," one X user posted earlier this week in a now-viral post with more than 1 million views.

Amazing. It just means more in the SEC, baby! Frankly, it's brilliant. This is the sort of out-of-the-box thinking the Razorbacks could use on an offense that currently ranks 115th in the country. Or a defense that ranks 108th and is currently giving up nearly 30 points per game.

SOUTH CAROLINA FOOTBALL IN FREE FALL AS SHANE BEAMER MAY BE OUT OF TIME WITH BUYOUT DECISION LOOMING

Just a thought.

Look, it probably won't happen but ... never say never. Razorback fans are tired. It's been a long few years, and that's an understatement.

Arkansas went 2-10 last season, and that wass the third such 2-10 campaign in the last decade. Just an absurd stat for an SEC school. It's unfathomable.

Somehow, it gets worse.

The Razorbacks haven't won 10 games since 2011, and have just one 9-win season (2021) in that same span. Growing up, Vanderbilt was the SEC bottom-feeder. Everyone knew it. That game was an automatic win when you looked at the preseason schedule.

Not anymore.

Arkansas has officially taken that spot, and it's probably going to get worse (somehow) before it gets better.

Perhaps fans storming the field — win or lose — and costing the program a hefty $250,000 fine each time they do so (per the NCAA rules) will expedite that process?

item.title: Stomach-turning sexually transmitted infection is on the rise — and standard medicines are failing
item.description: Shigella bacteria are becoming harder to treat as drug-resistant strains rise, and doctors warn Americans should be concerned but not panicked.
item.content:encoded:
A highly contagious gut infection that can spread during sex is becoming harder to treat as antibiotic-resistant strains become more common.

An April report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention tracked nearly 17,000 Shigella samples, which causes Shigellosis, which and can bring on diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps, collected between 2011 and 2023. In 2023, 8.5% of Shigella samples with resistance data were classified as extensively drug-resistant, or XDR — resistant to all five antibiotics in the CDC’s definition — compared with none from 2011 to 2015.

The findings point to a growing resistance problem, not a surge in overall infections, noted Dr. Tyler Evans, a California-based infectious disease physician and CEO of Wellness Equity Alliance.

HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS STOMACH BUG SPREADS FAST, HITTING CERTAIN PATIENTS HARDEST

"The infection is not surging. The bacteria are changing," Evans told Fox News Digital. "Case counts can hold steady while the treatment options quietly disappear."

There is no FDA-approved oral antibiotic for XDR Shigella, he said.

Shigella bacteria can spread when tiny amounts of stool reach someone's mouth, including through contaminated food or water, unwashed hands or sexual activity.

DANGEROUS DRUG-RESISTANT FUNGUS SPREADS ACROSS US, REACHING 27 STATES

"Shigella is not considered to be a typical sexually transmitted infection," Dr. Andi Toufexis, a Texas-based family medicine physician who specializes in sexual health, told Fox News Digital. "However, this gastrointestinal bacteria can be spread through sex when one partner comes into contact with the other's fecal matter."

Shigella is not new, and sexual transmission has been documented since the 1970s, Toufexis said. What is changing is the growing share of tested samples classified as XDR.

MICHIGAN REPORTS 2 DEATHS IN RARE PARASITE OUTBREAK THAT HAS SICKENED MORE THAN 11,000

The CDC report found that most people with XDR Shigella were adult men. Sexual exposure data were not routinely collected, so the report could not establish exactly how each infection was contracted but previous research has found sexual contact among men who have sex with men as an important transmission route.

Eighty-six percent of XDR patients were men, with a median age of 41, and of those with a known HIV status, nearly half were living with HIV, Evans noted. People experiencing homelessness and those with weakened immune systems may also face heightened risks, he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Children younger than 5 are especially likely to get Shigella, according to the CDC, and many outbreaks in the U.S. have been linked to child care and schools. Earlier U.S. outbreaks primarily affected children and involved strains that were susceptible to antibiotics.

According to the CDC report, 37.6% of patients with hospitalization data were hospitalized for the antibiotic-resistant infection. The CDC reported no deaths among the XDR cases analyzed and said infections may be undercounted because not all positive specimens were cultured or tested for resistance. Most patients with available travel histories reported no recent international travel, though travel information was missing for many.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Evans said Americans should be "concerned, not panicked" about the infection.

Most Shigella infections resolve on their own, Toufexis added, but severe illness may need treatment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Dr. Michael Aziz, an internist at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City and author of "The Perfect 10 Diet" and "The Ageless Revolution," urged people who suspect Shigella to seek medical advice before taking antidiarrheal medicine such as Imodium. "You want to flush out the bacteria, you want to get it out of your system," Aziz told Fox News Digital.

To reduce the chance of infection, doctors recommend washing hands, genitals and the anal area before and after sex, using condoms or dental dams, and cleaning sex toys after each use. If you or a partner has diarrhea, avoid sex and wait at least two weeks after symptoms end before resuming, Toufexis said.

"Feeling better does not always mean that an infection is completely gone," she said.

item.title: California Democrat 'deeply disappointed' after Newsom vetoes reparations tax break
item.description: Assemblymember Tina McKinnor says she is "deeply disappointed" after Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed her California reparations tax exemption.
item.content:encoded:
A California lawmaker told Fox News Digital that she is "deeply disappointed" after Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom vetoed her bill that would have exempted future reparations payments from California's personal income tax.

"I am deeply disappointed that Governor Newsom vetoed AB 2186. Reparations are not a gift or a government handout," Assemblymember Tina McKinnor, D-Inglewood, told Fox News Digital in a statement. "Reparations are meant to repair harm, not be partially taken back through taxation."

Newsom vetoed the measure on Sept. 30 as he acted on a series of bills, including other reparations-related legislation.

REPARATIONS ADVOCATES SLAM CASH COMPENSATION ‘HANDOUT’ LABEL, POINT TO PAST GOVERNMENT REMEDIES

In his official veto message, Newsom acknowledged the bill's intent but cited fiscal uncertainty.

"I thank the author for her continued work to redress the documented harms of slavery," Newsom wrote. "I was proud to sign into law last year legislation establishing the Bureau for Descendants of American Slavery, a first-in-the-nation law establishing a state agency that, among its key responsibilities, will advise on reparative justice programs for Black Americans. California's work on this important endeavor is just beginning."

Newsom also cited uncertainty about the potential cost of the exemption.

"Because the full scope of the proposed tax exclusion is unknown, fiscal caution is warranted," Newsom added. "The proposed exclusion for unspecified federal initiatives could be interpreted broadly, resulting in substantial fiscal uncertainty. Moreover, given the potentially significant General Fund implications, this measure should be considered as part of the annual budget process."

CALIFORNIA COUNTY APPROVES REPARATIONS PLAN AS NEIGHBORING SCHOOL DISTRICT 'BLACK THRIVING' EFFORT STALLS

Despite rejecting the tax exemption, Newsom signed another reparations-related measure into law. The first-in-the-nation law requires large companies doing business in California to scour historical records and publicly disclose slavery-era transactions, advancing the state's broader reparations push through a new corporate mandate.

Assembly Bill 2599, authored by Assemblymember Isaac Bryan, D-Ladera Heights, applies to businesses with more than $100 million in annual worldwide gross receipts that existed—or have a predecessor entity that existed—on or before Dec. 31, 1964. Once funded by the Legislature, covered companies must submit sworn affidavits under penalty of perjury verifying searches for historical records involving the purchase or sale of enslaved people, their use as loan collateral, slave-related insurance policies, and other transactions. Covered companies will have until January 2029 to submit their first affidavits.

CASH PAYMENTS ARE NOT 'RULED OUT' AS CALIFORNIA COUNTY OFFICIALS PUSH REPARATIONS FOR BLACK LOCALS

McKinnor's measure, Assembly Bill 2186, was designed to exempt future reparations payments or benefits from California's personal income tax if qualifying state, local or federal reparations programs were established.

Under the text of AB 2186, gross income would not have included "any reparations benefit or payment received by a taxpayer during the taxable year" for taxable years beginning on or after Jan. 1, 2028, and before Jan. 1, 2033. The bill defined a "reparations benefit or payment" as any monetary payment, grant, trust distribution, debt forgiveness, or other financial compensation provided through a qualifying reparations program.

SOME BLACK NEW YORKERS DEMAND CASH PAYMENTS AS ONLY 'TRUE' FORM OF JUSTICE

McKinnor emphasized that reparations payments are intended as compensation for generations of structural harm.

"Reparations payments are compensation for generations of injustice, discrimination, and economic harm," McKinnor said. "California cannot claim to support reparative justice while taxing the very compensation intended to repair that harm. I respect the Governor's concerns about fiscal responsibility, but justice must also be a priority."

"We cannot continue to study injustice, acknowledge the harm, and then hesitate when it is time to act," she added. "I remain committed to working with my colleagues and the new Governor to bring this legislation back in 2027. Justice delayed should not become justice denied."

California was the first state in the nation to establish a formal task force to study the legacy of slavery and recommend potential restitution measures. However, concrete direct-cash payout initiatives at the state level have stalled over budget concerns and legal vulnerabilities.

CHICAGO SUBURB EXPANDS CASH HANDOUTS AS RACE-BASED REPARATIONS PROGRAM FACES MAJOR LEGAL BATTLE

Elsewhere in the country, localized reparations programs have moved forward with mixed success. Black residents in Evanston, Illinois, received $25,000 housing grants as part of a municipal program aimed at rectifying historic housing discrimination. Similar local and municipal initiative seeking to provide direct compensation or economic aid are being debated nationwide.

The broader future of state-funded reparations in California remains highly precarious. With Newsom vetoing multiple reparations proposals citing fiscal parameters and legal challenges, and with the upcoming gubernatorial race featuring candidates reluctant to endorse broad direct cash handouts, the state's path toward financial restitution remains uncertain.

When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Newsom's office said that "the veto message speaks for itself."

item.title: Who is Sally Yates? Cornell rape-review pick was fired by Trump after refusing to defend travel ban
item.description: Sally Yates, fired by Trump as acting attorney general in 2017, will now lead Cornell University's independent review of sexual assault policies.
item.content:encoded:
Cornell University has tapped Sally Yates, a former Obama administration deputy attorney general fired by President Donald Trump during his first term, to lead an independent review of the Ivy League school's handling of sexual assault allegations.

Yates' appointment comes as Cornell faces scrutiny over its response to an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house in October 2024. As part of the independent review, Yates and her employer, King & Spalding, will have access to Cornell's internal documents, including case files, oversight records for Greek organizations, communications with law enforcement and disciplinary hearing records.

Yates brings decades of Justice Department experience to Cornell's review, along with a public profile shaped by her confrontation with Trump and subsequent involvement in the Russia investigation.

President Barack Obama nominated Yates as deputy attorney general in January 2015, and the Senate confirmed her four months later in an 84-12 vote. She previously served as U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Georgia, a position Obama appointed her to in 2010.

CORNELL PRESIDENT SAYS UNIVERSITY 'MUST DO BETTER' ON HANDLING OF SEXUAL ASSAULT ALLEGATIONS

During the presidential transition, Trump's incoming administration asked Yates to remain as acting attorney general while his nominee, Jeff Sessions, awaited Senate confirmation. But her tenure lasted just 10 days.

Trump fired Yates on Jan. 30, 2017, after she instructed Justice Department lawyers not to defend his executive order restricting travel and refugee admissions from seven predominantly Muslim countries.

"The acting Attorney General, Sally Yates, has betrayed the Department of Justice by refusing to enforce a legal order designed to protect the citizens of the United States," the White House said in a statement announcing her firing.

Yates maintained that she was not convinced the directive was lawful.

"My responsibility is to ensure that the position of the Department of Justice is not only legally defensible, but is informed by our best view of what the law is after consideration of all the facts," Yates said in a letter. "In addition, I am responsible for ensuring that the positions we take in court remain consistent with this institution’s solemn obligation to always seek justice and stand for what is right."

Yates returned to the national spotlight in May 2017, testifying before a Senate Judiciary subcommittee investigating Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election. Her testimony detailed warnings she had given White House Counsel Don McGahn about Trump's then-national security adviser, Michael Flynn, shortly before her dismissal.

CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS PROMPT NY ATTORNEY GENERAL LETITIA JAMES TO OPEN ‘ACTIVE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION’

Flynn had discussed Obama administration sanctions against Russia with Russian Ambassador Sergey Kislyak in December 2016, despite then-Vice President-elect Mike Pence publicly denying that sanctions were discussed.

After reviewing FBI intelligence, Yates warned McGahn that Flynn had misled administration officials and could be vulnerable to Russian blackmail because Moscow knew what had actually been discussed.

Flynn resigned in February 2017, 18 days after Yates' initial warning. He later pleaded guilty to making false statements to the FBI about his conversations with Kislyak.

Before her confrontation with Trump, Yates spent 27 years at the Justice Department, prosecuting white-collar fraud and public corruption cases. She also served as lead prosecutor in the case against Olympic Park bomber Eric Rudolph, a prosecution then-Attorney General Eric Holder highlighted when Obama selected her as deputy attorney general.

Yates returned to King & Spalding as a partner in May 2018, later leading an independent investigation into sexual misconduct and abuse in the National Women's Soccer League.

Commissioned by the U.S. Soccer Federation in October 2021, the investigation included more than 200 interviews and uncovered widespread verbal and emotional abuse, sexual misconduct and repeated failures by teams and league officials to address complaints.

The findings, released in October 2022, documented how coaches accused of misconduct continued working despite previous complaints. Yates' report recommended stronger background checks, clearer reporting procedures and greater accountability for teams and league officials.

Cornell said it selected Yates and her firm because of "their expertise in higher education and extensive experience conducting independent investigations for boards and institutions."

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Yates' involvement in the case brings another prominent Trump adversary into the controversy, days after New York Attorney General Letitia James, who previously brought a civil fraud case against Trump and has faced his calls for her prosecution, was appointed to oversee a separate state investigation.

Cornell previously investigated the alleged assault and imposed suspensions and expulsions on several students accused of involvement. A lawsuit filed against the university by the alleged victim has since brought renewed national attention to the case and raised questions about the school's response.

The two investigations have separate mandates. James' investigation will examine the case at the center of the controversy, while Yates' review will assess Cornell's broader policies and handling of sexual assault and dating violence allegations.

"As part of that broader mandate, Yates and her team will conduct a detailed review of the university’s response to the allegations involving Jane Doe and members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024, including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter," the school said in a statement.

Fox News Digital reached out to Yates for comment.

item.title: Journey drummer rushed to hospital after medical emergency interrupts concert
item.description: Journey's Tulsa concert stopped after just two songs when drummer Deen Castronovo suffered a medical emergency, with bandmates asking for prayers.
item.content:encoded:
Journey drummer Deen Castronovo was taken to a hospital Thursday after suffering a medical emergency during the band's concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

The group stopped the show after just two songs as his bandmates asked fans to pray for him.

Castronovo, 62, was transported to a hospital after leaving the stage, according to video shared on X.

Keyboardist Jonathan Cain addressed the crowd, apologizing for the interruption while urging fans to keep the drummer in their prayers.

LIONEL RICHIE HOSPITALIZED IN ST LOUIS AFTER SUMMER OF HEALTH SCARES AND CANCELED CONCERTS

"We're going to see what happens as this progresses," Cain explained. "It's an unfortunate situation. We're very sorry. We're hoping it's only a delay, but please — I'm sorry. Don't worry. Have your prayers ready. Have your prayers ready for Deen Castronovo, everybody. Thank you."

Guitarist Neal Schon then stepped forward to explain how the band planned to continue the concert, according to local outlet Tulsa World.

JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK

Schon said Castronovo was being taken to the hospital and confirmed the concert would continue with the band's longtime drum technician, Steve Toomey, taking over behind the kit.

"Please give a big hand for Steve Toomey. We'll be back in about 15 minutes. We love you all, we're really sorry about the inconvenience," Schon said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The band returned to the stage after the interruption, with lead singer Arnel Pineda offering a reassuring message despite the lack of publicly confirmed details about Castronovo's condition.

"He's gonna be fine. Too much Gatorade," Pineda said, according to Ultimate Classic Rock.

Schon later dedicated the performance to his bandmate and expressed hope that Castronovo would recover.

"This concert's for Deen tonight. I'd love you all to pray for him. Everybody's been going through a lot. I think he's going to be fine," Schon said.

The cause of the medical emergency has not been publicly disclosed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Journey's representatives for comment.

The medical scare comes as Journey makes its way through the fall dates of its "Final Frontier Tour," the band's farewell tour.

The tour features Schon and Cain alongside Pineda, Castronovo, keyboardist Jason Derlatka and bassist Todd Jensen. The North American run kicked off in February, and the tour is scheduled to conclude Nov. 28 in San Francisco.

Schon has previously described the tour as a celebration of Journey's music and the fans who have supported the band for generations.

"The music we’ve created together is amazing. And so, you have to celebrate that music with the fans. The fans are incredible," Schon told Rolling Stone.

item.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. informed he's being traded as Cardinals seek a second-round pick in return
item.description: Marvin Harrison Jr. was told the Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade, with the Texans, Chiefs, Eagles and Bills among teams pursuing him.
item.content:encoded:
Marvin Harrison Jr.'s time with the Arizona Cardinals is coming to an end after it began only three seasons ago as a first-round draft pick with a Hall of Fame pedigree and high expectations.

The team has informed Harrison it is finalizing a deal to trade him and he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Detriot Lions, ESPN first reported and OutKick has confirmed.

Harrison was not initially told what team he'd be traded to, perhaps, one NFL source said, because the Cardinals were open to the idea of having the news leak, and then other teams would raise their trade offers for Harrison.

CARDINALS' MARVIN HARRISON JR LOOKS ENTIRELY DISINTERESTED AS SEASON GETS OFF TO A PUTRID START

But he's definitely going somewhere else.

Harrison, the son of Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, was the fourth player taken in the 2024 NFL Draft ahead of multiple starting quarterbacks and more productive players such as Brock Bowers, but he has fallen out of favor over the last year as his production declined, his effort and even body language around the team has been questioned and other teams showed interest in acquiring him.

CAN MARVIN HARRISON JR. AND TREY MCBRIDE CARRY THE CARDINALS OFFENSE UNDER NEW COACH MIKE LAFLEUR?

New coach Mike LaFleur had defended Harrison's effort, saying, "I don’t see it that way. I think his running style is different than some other people’s," while adding that other players had increasingly more defined roles in an offense with limited weekly plays.

LaFleur also said some opportunities for Harrison have been eliminated because defensive coverages have dictated he not get the ball while Arizona’s own subpar quarterback play also hasn't helped.

The problem with that is the Cardinals have had great receivers who have dealt with similar issues and they were very much valued. Hall of Famer Larry Fitzgerald comes to mind.

Except Fitzgerald was never inconsistent in his pass catching while Harrison has struggled with drops. And Fitzgerald simply played hard – all the time. Harrison?

It's a lingering question.

Rumors of a possible Harrison trade have persisted for weeks, fed by the fact he is eligible for a contract extension after this season and the Cardinals may not be convinced Harrison is worthy of a big contract. Also, Michael Wilson has emerged as a more productive receiver while Harrison currently ranks only fifth on the team in targets.

General manager Monti Ossenfort said on Oct. 9 that Harrison "is a big part of what we’re doing," suggesting the team is still more interested in fixing his situation than moving him.

Nope.

Harrison Jr. wasn't immediately a bust after being drafted out of Ohio State. His rookie season showed both his talent and some inconsistency, but he finished with 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns.

The Cardinals expected a Year 2 jump from Harrison. That never came and didn't come this season, either.

Multiple teams have contacted the Cardinals about Harrison.

The Houston Texans have, the Kansas City Chiefs have, as have the Philadelphia Eagles, Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots, and even the San Francisco 49ers – although that last one is a long shot considering they play in the same division with the Cardinals.

The Cardinals have been seeking a package that included a second-round pick in return for Harrison.

And this is how bad teams stay bad: The Cardinals are essentially trading a 2024 first round pick for a second-rounder (maybe) years later after getting little in return for their initial investment.

item.title: Letitia James faces new push to boot her from Cornell rape probe over alleged bias: court docs
item.description: A defense lawyer argues New York Attorney General Letitia James prejudged the Cornell University rape case and asks Tompkins County court to remove her.
item.content:encoded:
A lawyer representing one of the men accused in a civil lawsuit of raping Cornell University's "Jane Doe" has formally requested that New York Attorney General Letitia James be removed from the criminal investigation, alleging she is biased and prejudged the case before being appointed as special prosecutor.

Teny Geragos, daughter of prominent criminal defense attorney Mark Geragos, filed a motion Thursday in Tompkins County court arguing that James' previous public statements in support of the accuser have "prejudiced grand jurors."

The motion cited a social media post made by James on Sept. 28, the same day local prosecutor Matthew Van Houten announced he would be reopening the case.

"What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers," James wrote. "To her, and to all survivors: you’re not alone. We stand with you."

CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE

Geragos argued that this showed James believed the seven men in the fraternity who were named in the prior civil lawsuit were guilty "despite not having examined a shred of evidence" up to that point.

"The public cannot, and should not, have any confidence in the investigation or charging decisions of someone who has clearly prejudged the guilt of individuals who the law presumes are innocent," Geragos wrote in the filing. "The AG should be removed."

She also accused New York Governor Kathy Hochul of selecting James because of her "prejudicial public statements" about the case, arguing that the governor expects the investigation to produce a particular outcome.

AOC'S DRAMATIC RETELLING OF CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS COLLIDES WITH COMPLAINT DETAILS

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Hochul referred Fox News Digital to the governor's answer to a reporter's question about James' social media post at an Oct. 2 press conference.

"I will answer that. I have every confidence in our Attorney General to do what she has always done: look at the facts, examine the record and draw the proper conclusions. That's exactly what's going to happen in this case," Hochul said.

The attorney general's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Geragos' motion comes days after another one of the men named in the civil suit filed a request in Albany State Supreme Court seeking James's removal, also citing alleged bias.

The former Cornell student at the center of the investigation filed the civil lawsuit in September accusing seven former Chi Phi fraternity members of drugging and raping her on the night of Oct. 19, 2024, and into the following morning.

In the lawsuit, she alleges she arrived at the frat house already intoxicated, after which the men pressured her into taking ketamine and other substances. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated.

The fraternity was suspended on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day Doe reported sexual assault allegations to campus police, according to Doe's civil complaint.

Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said Doe's November 2024 sworn statement did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped and, instead, described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."

item.title: Country star Drew Baldridge lifts curtain on Jelly Roll's 'wild' entourage, Luke Bryan's 'country boy' life
item.description: Drew Baldridge reveals why Jelly Roll's backstage scene is wildly unpredictable and how Luke Bryan's dove-hunting trips show his country roots.
item.content:encoded:
Country music superstars may share the spotlight, but their lives behind the scenes can look very different.

Drew Baldridge, who recently released his album, "FARM FAITH FAMILY," got a front-row seat to both worlds — from Luke Bryan's down-home lifestyle to Jelly Roll's jam-packed backstage scene, where the next unexpected guest could be just around the corner.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Baldridge shared details about what the country hitmakers are really like offstage, revealing why Bryan's humble roots and devotion to his family have stuck with him — and why Jelly Roll's backstage operation is anything but predictable.

JELLY ROLL SAYS HE COULD WALK AWAY FROM COUNTRY MUSIC IF GOD TELLS HIM TO: ‘Y’ALL WILL NEVER SEE ME AGAIN’

When it comes to the wildest backstage setup in country music, Baldridge knows who gets his vote.

"Oh man, I don't know what the weirdest rider thing is, but Jelly probably has the wildest backstage, because you just never know who's going to be there," he said.

According to Baldridge, Jelly Roll’s backstage crowd can rival the audience out front.

"I mean, you walk in … it is like a stadium full of people out front, but there's a stadium full of people in the back," he said.

LUKE COMBS SAYS ‘WHO THE F--- CARES’ IF CHOOSING FAMILY TIME OVER INDUSTRY PARTIES COSTS HIM AWARDS

The singer said Jelly Roll's welcoming nature attracts all kinds of guests, including influencers looking to capture extra content after the show.

"My goodness, this guy is always on," Baldridge said. "And always has just an entourage of people, that is for sure."

WATCH: COUNTRY STAR DREW BALDRIDGE DISHES ON JELLY ROLL'S WILD ENTOURAGE

Meanwhile, Bryan’s offstage life offers a different kind of surprise, Baldridge said.

"Luke is just like one of my buddies I would grow up with," he said, adding that fame has not altered the superstar's personality.

"You'd think all the success that he had that he would change who he is or anything, but that dude's just a country boy."

Baldridge said he recently visited Bryan for a dove-hunting trip, describing the experience as an afternoon spent with an old friend.

He said Bryan’s commitment to his family made an even bigger impression, particularly his determination to attend his sons’ football games despite his busy touring schedule.

"Watching him never miss one of his son's football games, flying home and even taking off Friday night to make sure he was at his boy's game, not playing a show that night – that's been really cool, I think," Baldridge said.

The experience was especially meaningful because Bryan had been one of Baldridge's musical heroes since he was a teenager.

"Oh dang, he's just a country boy like I am, you know?" he said.

Baldridge is also embracing family life with two young children of his own, saying fatherhood has changed his perspective as he balances touring and recording.

"Definitely, family has changed the most. I have a five-month-old and a three-year-old," he said.

His 16-track major-label debut, "FARM FAITH FAMILY," reflects the three values that have shaped his life, with the album divided into sections devoted to farm life, faith and family.

The project includes "Let ‘Em," a song about his sons, and "A Man Don't," which explores his views on manhood, faith and marriage.

"That has definitely been a whirlwind, balancing this musical career and also the family life of being a dad and a husband and figuring that out every day," he said.

Baldridge broke through with "She's Somebody's Daughter," an RIAA Platinum-certified hit that reached No. 1 on the Country Aircheck/Mediabase chart and No. 3 on Billboard's Country Airplay chart.

item.title: Inside Hasan Piker’s radical views on America, Israel and socialism
item.description: Hasan Piker's critics claimed his Marxist worldview goes beyond progressivism, casting America as fundamentally corrupt and worse than al-Qaeda.
item.content:encoded:
Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has built his online brand through intense commentary on political topics ranging from economics to foreign policy. During his daily streams, which last several hours, he gives his takes on the issues of the day, often through a combative left-wing lens.

As Piker's influence has moved from his online audience and into the real world, including Democratic politics and campus events, critics argue his ideology deserves more scrutiny.

To his supporters, Piker is an effective messenger for a generation looking for something outside traditional political structures. However, multiple critics who spoke with Fox News Digital described the streamer's worldview as going beyond typical progressive and anti-establishment outlooks. They claim his beliefs cast America as fundamentally corrupt, treat socialism as the answer to economic frustrations and frame Israel as uniquely immoral and illegitimate.

WHO IS HASAN PIKER? MEET THE FAR-LEFT STREAMER WHO IS STIRRING UP CONTROVERSY AND DIVIDING DEMOCRATS

Eli Lake, a senior reporter at The Free Press and host of the podcast "Breaking History," told Fox News Digital that Piker's belief system is "informed in many ways by a Marxist view of history" and that the streamer is part of "a tradition of the anti-American left."

"There is a tradition of elements of the Left that believes that the country and the republic are rotten to its core, and I think that that is a distinction from, you know, a more kind of hopeful version of progressivism," Lake told Fox News Digital.

Lake contrasted Piker's beliefs with a reform-minded view in which the Declaration of Independence serves as a starting point from which the U.S. would progress. The goal, according to Lake, would be to hold the country to its stated ideals, an approach that he said is "distinct from the way that Hasan Piker understands the United States as sort of irredeemably evil."

In one of Piker's more recent controversial statements, the streamer said in an interview with Axios that the U.S. was worse than al-Qaeda.

"Pound for pound as far as the number of deaths, yes," Piker told Axios. "We have caused tremendous terror all around the world."

Lake criticized Piker's remarks in an article for The Free Press, writing that the streamer's inability to "to grasp the distinction between intentionally and unintentionally killing civilians" showed his "moral illiteracy."

HASAN PIKER ADMITS HE HAS 'DIALED DOWN' HIS OPINIONS AFTER PUBLIC AND DEMOCRATIC BACKLASH

"I almost felt guilty writing a column because I could assume it was so obvious that America is nothing like al-Qaeda. Al-Qaeda deliberately is trying to kill as many civilians as it can," Lake told Fox News Digital. "If Hasan Piker cannot distinguish between America and its foreign policy and that of al-Qaeda in a moral sense at least, or he thinks they're equal or 'pound for pound' America is worse, then he's helpless."

Piker's critics argue that his moral framework also shapes his views of Israel. They say that he goes beyond criticizing the Israeli government or its policies and frames the Jewish state's existence as being up for debate, something that Tanya Tsikanovsky, a first-generation American whose parents fled the Soviet Union, takes issue with.

"I think that we can sit here and discuss the government of Israel, but we're not citizens of Israel. Certainly Hasan Piker is not, and we don't live there," Tsikanovsky told Fox News Digital. "As a Zionist, and as someone who is a proud jew, I'm here to care about the existence of the state. I just want it to exist."

She also pointed out that Piker does not apply the same standards he has for Israel to other countries.

"You know we don't spend our time debating the existence of any other country. Like Hasan's not saying, 'Maybe Switzerland shouldn't really be a country.' No, like, we're good with every other country," she said, adding that, in her view, the reason for this singling out of Israel is antisemitism.

Tsikanovsky told Fox News Digital that her immigrant parents view the country in an entirely different light from Piker. She said that they see the U.S. as a place where they were finally able to be free and live as equals.

"My parents came here from the USSR, and they kiss the ground of this country because we know that it's the best country on Earth," she said. "There really is no other place in the world that provides the same level of freedom, and Hassan Piker is using that freedom specifically to get everyone to want to lose it and without even realizing it."

She argued that Piker's worldview is hostile to the American system and that it welcomes the exact things that families like hers fled.

FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM ANTISEMITISM ACCUSATIONS IN INTERVIEW WITH JEWISH OUTLET

"[Piker] is aligning himself with an ideology that will embrace Sharia law, that will embrace communism," she said.

Piker's critics say his worldview is not merely defined by what he opposes, but also the economic system he promotes.

Venezuelan-born economist Daniel Di Martino argued that there is a hidden danger to Piker's economic stances, mainly the appeal of socialist promises to young people frustrated with capitalism.

Di Martino, who grew up in Venezuela before immigrating to the U.S., said that socialism was more than an abstract idea, it was a system that made ordinary life substantially worse. He described growing up under socialism as "feeling the constant deterioration of my quality of life in even the daily smallest things."

Recently, Piker took the 12 Axes political test on one of his daily streams, and the results showed that he was closely aligned economically with late Venezuelan socialist leader Hugo Chávez, something Di Martino saw as a significant red flag.

"Their economic policies are not those of Norway and Denmark. They're the ones of Venezuela. They are the ones that destroy the country I come from," Di Martino said.

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA BACKS 'OUR TWITCH STREAMER' HASAN PIKER, RIPS ANTI-SOCIALISM HOUSE RESOLUTION

He recalled Venezuela unraveling before his eyes as the government began using state resources to provide free goods and services. When oil money was no longer enough, Di Martino said, the government printed money, fueling inflation. Eventually, shortages came and Di Martino recalled the government blaming business owners for being greedy and claiming that citizens were hoarding food.

"They hailed bread lines and shortages as evidence that there was so much demand because Venezuelans were so well off. I mean, imagine how laughable these arguments [were]," Di Martino told Fox News Digital.

"And eventually they said that inflation was imaginary, it was all made up in our heads. And then we had no electricity, and then we have no water," he added. "And then crime went up and it went unpunished. And then they jailed their political opponents when they tried to speak up, and then they rigged the elections because that is the only way for socialists to stay in power, because it always fails, so they have to rig the elections to stay in power."

For Di Martino, the real danger of Piker's growing influence is not simply that he has a large online audience, but that his ideas are moving into Democratic politics and could eventually shape U.S. government policy.

"Even though he's not running, the people running on the socialist side, the democratic socialist candidates, listen to him and have his ideas, which are Marxist-Leninist ideas, are the ideas of the Chinese Communist Party — which is why he goes there — are the ideas of the socialist party of Venezuela, of the communist party of Cuba. That is what these people stand for," Di Martino said. "And so, we should be worried, not because Hassan Piker is popular, he is not, we should be worried because his ideas are gonna make it to the Congress and to the state and local governments."

Piker's critics are not merely concerned with the provocative things he says regularly online, but that his platform is reaching a group of voters that the left has tried to court. In their eyes, this could mean the adoption of hard-left politics in the government, putting the very idea of the American system at risk.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Katie Zacharia hits ground running, promises Trump diesel deal delivers cheaper gas for Americans

item.content:encoded:
Incoming White House press secretary Katie Zacharia pledged to get to work immediately when she takes over the podium on Monday, defending President Donald Trump's recent diesel deal as a move she says will help lower gas and grocery prices.

Speaking on "Fox & Friends Weekend," Zacharia said Trump is using a "multifaceted" approach to tackle inflation while balancing U.S. interests overseas.

"President Trump has heard people have been frustrated with the gas prices. People are frustrated with the increasing grocery prices. And he is delivering what he always does, which are solutions," Zacharia said Saturday.

TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA

"President Donald Trump has never been unambiguous. He is an America-first president. He is putting [American interests] first, American citizens first with this deal. And we will have cheaper gas, cheaper groceries with this diesel deal," she added.

The president announced Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to "immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter."

TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA

Diesel prices have remained high as conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine continue, with rising fuel costs emerging as an issue ahead of November's midterm elections. Zacharia suggested that the diesel deal could also help advance peace efforts between Ukraine and Russia.

"He did it with Venezuela, and he did it with—he's doing it with Canada and did it in Greenland. So, I think we're [going to] see some historic wins, and President Trump is [going to] deliver that," she said.

TRUMP TOUTS ACCESS TO 65 BILLION BARRELS OF VENEZUELAN OIL IN DEAL HE SAYS WILL SLASH GAS PRICES

The incoming press secretary then shifted her focus to November's midterm elections. She argued the president has "delivered historic results," but said congressional Republicans could have accomplished more by passing key legislation, including the SAVE America Act.

"I would have loved to see more from our congressional Republicans in the Senate. I think President Trump has done everything in his power to do that," Zacharia said.

LEE CARTER: POLLS SAY DEMOCRATS COULD SWAMP REPUBLICANS. AS A POLLSTER, I HAVE A QUESTION

Her Saturday morning comments followed a Friday night appearance on "Jesse Watters Primetime," during which Zacharia criticized Democratic campaign strategies, accusing the party of keeping candidates she considers weak out of the public eye.

"This is what happened with Joe Biden, basement Joe, for the 2020 election. We didn't see him until we had to," Zacharia told Watters.

"They think they can hide these candidates and we won't notice," she added.

Zacharia pointed to California gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico as examples of figures she believes Democrats are keeping out of the spotlight.

LEE CARTER: TRUMP CAN STILL GET ATTENTION, CAN HE DISTRACT VOTERS FROM THEIR BILLS?

"Becerra's disappeared, Talarico disappeared. And it's on purpose because they know they can't continue letting them talk because they're destroying their campaigns," Zacharia said.

Talarico reappeared on the campaign trail Friday after a nearly two-week absence, ending days of speculation. 

Zacharia also revealed how she learned of her White House appointment, telling Watters that Trump personally called her with the news.

"I got a wonderful phone call from the chief talent recruiter, the president himself," she said. "He loved what a fighter I was for him... I just get to continue doing what I've been doing, which is promote all of the things that President Trump is doing on behalf of the American people."

Trump announced Zacharia's appointment on Friday, writing on Truth Social: "It is my Great Honor to have just appointed, as Press Secretary, Katie Zacharia. Katie currently serves as Senior Communications Advisor to Truth Social (Trump Media & Technology Group), where she has been outstanding!"

LEAVITT PULLS BACK THE CURTAIN ON TRUMP'S 'TENSE,' UNFILTERED PRIVATE TALKS WITH PUTIN, XI, STARMER

"She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA! I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration," he added.

Fox News Digital's Brie Stimson, Louis Casiano and Brooke Taylor contributed to this report.

item.title: ABC News quietly republishes gutted version of story on Trump sons it had deleted without explanation
item.description: ABC News issued an editor's note admitting errors in its report on Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump's investments tied to Pentagon contracts.
item.content:encoded:
ABC News quietly republished a watered-down version of a previously deleted report scrutinizing the business dealings of President Donald Trump's oldest sons, Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, on Friday evening. The original report, published earlier in the week, was removed following criticism of its accuracy.

The original report, which remains accessible through the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine, was published Wednesday afternoon under the headline, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election." ABC News removed the report less than 24 hours later without a public explanation at the time.

However, the revised report reappeared on ABC News' website Friday with an editor's note, factual corrections and a new headline: "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest."

ABC NEWS DELETES ‘HIT PIECE’ ON TRUMP SONS' PENTAGON-LINKED INVESTMENTS WITHOUT EXPLANATION

The article's byline was also changed to "ABC News."

The editor's note acknowledged errors involving descriptions of company investments, government contracts and the chronology of events.

ABC News' decision to remove the report without an immediate public explanation drew criticism from media industry figures.

ABC News' revisions followed public criticism from 1789 Capital spokesperson Alexa Henning, who disputed the original report's description of the firm's investments. Henning said "1789 Capital does not have a 'major stake' in Anduril" and challenged the article's characterization of the Trump brothers' involvement in other companies.

"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning wrote.

1789 Capital is the venture firm in which Trump Jr. serves as a partner.

The initial report incorrectly attributed a $2.5 billion investment in Anduril to 1789 Capital. The revised article clarified that the figure represented the total funding Anduril raised last year.

INSIDE TRUMP’S DEAL TO GIVE AMERICAN TAXPAYERS A MASSIVE STAKE IN NEW $6.6B SUBMARINE DEAL

"1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company," ABC News reported in the deleted story.

The revised article also states that Trump Jr. does not sit on the three-person committee responsible for investment decisions, according to a spokesperson for 1789 Capital.

The updated story states that 1789 Capital previously invested $50 million in defense contractor Anduril, which ABC valued at approximately $60 billion.

The initial removal drew the attention of Trump Jr., who took to X to mock California Gov. Gavin Newsom after the story was taken down.

"ABC deleted this article in less than 24 hours because it’s false. Sounds about as long as your presidential campaign would last," he wrote on X.

Bill Ackman, founder and CEO of Pershing Square Capital Management, criticized ABC News on social media for removing the article without issuing a public correction at the time.

"This is bad. @ABC must take responsibility for their failed journalism. Basic journalistic ethics requires it," Ackman wrote on X. "A quiet unexplained withdrawal of a false article does not constitute a proper error correction."

Fox News Digital reached out to ABC News, Trump Jr. and 1789 Capital for comment.

item.title: LA Knight's 'do or die' moment comes at Money in the Bank against Roman Reigns with world title on the line
item.description: LA Knight faces Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship at Money in the Bank in what feels like a do-or-die moment for his career.
item.content:encoded:
The Money in the Bank premium live event represents the biggest opportunity for superstars to earn a world championship shot and even win a title on the same night.

It’s the luck of the draw. For six men and six women, all they have to do is climb the ladder, grab the briefcase and get the contract for a title match at any time. For others, the deck has been stacked against them for so long that the path to glory is more of a mirage than reality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

LA Knight won’t need a ladder on Saturday night. He won’t need to climb a mountain, either. All he will have to do is flip table in where Roman Reigns resides as the head of and win the World Heavyweight Championship. It’s easier to say and type that than it will be to complete the task. Reigns has been the world champion since he defeated CM Punk at WrestleMania 42. Reigns declared he would not be taking any time off and with that, he knocked down any challenger that has come forth.

It truly feels like it’s now or never for LA Knight.

Knight’s popularity rose in 2023. The LA summer propelled him into a top babyface but even after challenging Reigns for the title, he could never find a way to beat him. To Knight, he has been screwed out of those opportunities thanks to The Bloodline – Reigns’ faction of family members who have had his back through thick and thin. Jimmy Uso was the culprit who cost Knight the title at Crown Jewel in 2023. Knight was then thrust into a fatal four-way match at Royal Rumble 2024. Reigns pinned AJ Styles to retain the Undisputed WWE Championship at the time.

Knight’s pursuits shifted after that. He defeated Logan Paul at SummerSlam 2024 and later lost it to Shinsuke Nakamura at Survivor Series: War Games more than 100 days later. But the odor of The Bloodline continued to linger even if it was Solo Sikoa who took over as the makeshift leader for a period of time.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He had to fight, claw and even team with members of The Bloodline before getting back to Reigns. It was in Paris earlier this summer when Knight declared himself "unchosen" and put himself back on the path of the world heavyweight title.

"I may be unchosen, but every single one of you chose me," Knight said at the time. "And more importantly than any of that, I chose myself, which means I do it my way, which means I get the job done. And I make you one single, solitary promise, which is I don’t know how to quit. I don’t know how to stop. I can’t stop the undeniable kavorka and I can’t stop being L.A. Knight."

Doing it his way meant teaming with Sikoa and Royce Keys to topple Jimmy and Jey Uso and Jacob Fatu at SummerSlam in August. It meant waiting for Reigns to retain his title that same night. It meant waiting for the winner of Reigns vs. Penta in Mexico City last month.

Now, the wait is over. It’s now or never for Knight. If this doesn’t feel like the peak of what Knight is able to accomplish, then I’m not sure what is. He is among the most popular wrestlers on the WWE roster. He has the crowd behind him. He just needs the trigger pulled.

Knight said it himself on TMZ’s "Inside the Ring."

"So many people ask, like, how has LA Knight not been world champion yet?" he said. "It’s almost like, put up or shut up, do or die. This is the time to do it. And if it doesn’t happen here, it’s just kind of like, where do I go from here?"

It’s the big question that looms over Knight should he lose. There will be a new contender coming out of the men’s Money in the Bank ladder match immediately. The Raw roster is filled with championship-level talent, including Keys, Oba Femi and Bronson Reed outside those on the brand who are in the ladder match (Bron Breakker, Penta, Je’Von Evans).

Saturday night could very well be Knight’s last chance to win the title. Knight’s fans will be watching with bated breath to see if he can pull through. Luckily, there was at least one person on the record pulling for him – WWE Hall of Famer Diamond Dallas Page.

Page told OutKick Dropkick he was putting it into the universe that Knight will win.

"I would love to see that. I would love to see that … LA and I have been, because of our careers, even though he started wrestling in his 20s, our career took off in our 40s and I would love to see that. Do I believe it's going to happen? I'm going to say yes because I want it to be out in the universe for LA," Page said in a recent interview, on behalf of Gambling.com, the guide to the best online sportsbooks.

We all will have to wait and see if the odds are in his favor.

Knight has made a point to say in recent weeks, almost commendable, that Reigns has been able to defend his title without the help of The Bloodline. Reigns sent The Usos on a quest to keep Fatu in line but with the emergence of the 946 – things have gone completely off the rails.

Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price have sent pointed messages to The Usos and Fatu, which led to an all-out brawl. Jaida Parker then ran over Fatu with her car and signaled her allegiance to the 946. With The Bloodline preoccupied and Reigns seemingly rescuing Sikoa from the 946, one has to wonder whether the 946 will enter the fray.

Putting my fantasy book cap on for a second, I can see two other routes the World Heavyweight Championship match could go.

The first possibility is that Knight gets help from the 946. Keys could definitely cost Reigns the title, evolving the feud into November’s Survivor Series: WarGames. A branch from that could be Knight joining the 946. Let’s keep our antenna up for that just in case.

The other possibility is Sikoa screwing Knight over despite their supposed friendship. The two have cozied up over the last few months. But Knight made clear he really didn’t want to get into any of the 946 business.

Sikoa costing Knight and returning to The Bloodline as the "enforcer" is a real possibility. If Knight does lose on Saturday, that’s likely where his storyline will go. Did your lightbulb go off while reading that? Yeah, mine did too.

Whatever the case may be, Money in the Bank has the potential to be really chaotic.
